groups.0.entries.0.meaning.t: Layer 7 HTTP traffic filter that decides, per request, whether it proceeds, is challenged, is limited or is blocked. It reduces the exposed surface and enables virtual patching; it does not replace fixing the application.

groups.0.entries.1.meaning.t: Define what is valid for an endpoint (methods, paths, formats, sizes) and block everything else. More precise than signatures, but requires knowing the application.

groups.0.entries.2.meaning.t: Phase in which a rule runs in parallel without acting, and the simulated decision is compared with reality to measure false positives before enforcement.

groups.0.entries.3.meaning.t: WAF rule that blocks exploitation of a known vulnerability while the real fix has not yet reached the application. It buys time, it does not eliminate the flaw.

groups.0.entries.4.meaning.t: Limit on requests per entity and time window. The choice of key (IP, account, token, ASN) matters as much as the limit value.

groups.0.entries.5.meaning.t: Check that tries to prove the client is a real browser, without asking the user for anything in most cases. It is the step before blocking.

groups.0.entries.6.meaning.t: What the system does when a security control fails: fail-open lets traffic through (available, unprotected), fail-closed blocks it (safe, unavailable). The choice should be conscious, per endpoint.

groups.1.entries.0.meaning.t: Attack that tests leaked username/password pairs from other services at scale. Signature: many login failures spread across many IPs, with few attempts per account.

groups.1.entries.1.meaning.t: Distance of a value from the mean, measured in standard deviations. In detection, values far above the recent history of the same key suggest an anomaly.

groups.1.entries.2.meaning.t: Average that gives more weight to recent data. Used as an adaptive baseline: it follows changes in normal traffic without getting stuck in the past.

groups.1.entries.3.meaning.t: Number of distinct values in a field (IPs, user agents). High cardinality makes aggregations expensive and takes down metrics systems; aggregate at the coarsest level that still separates the attack from normal traffic.

groups.1.entries.4.meaning.t: Average time between the alert and its classification as real or false.

groups.1.entries.5.meaning.t: Average time between confirming an attack and containing it.

groups.1.entries.6.meaning.t: Precision: of the alerts issued, how many were real attacks. Recall: of the attacks that exist, how many were detected. Raising one tends to lower the other.
